heading: Suggested prompt cards
subheading: Student photographs · one mission per card
prompts: Why did you show us this?
promptsLine: Every photo gets three prompts, and only three: What is this? Why did you show us this? What were you doing? Plus the card’s own question.
optional: You can give the student prompts to guide what they photograph.
If you want the photographs to emerge with as little direction as possible, do not use them.
Choose the level of direction that suits your research.

captureStage.title: The capture stage
captureStage.lead: The kinds of data you need the student to capture
items: Why did you show us that?
captureStage.note: Each picture should have a context from their end.

output.title: Output of Show
output.body: A set of participant-generated images + participant accounts.
output.ready: You are ready to move on when you have enough images to begin seeing relationships or repetitions, not when you have “covered the whole environment.”

missions.title: Show me where you learn
missions.body: Show me something that helps you know what to do. A message, a notice, a person, a document, a screenshot, a handwritten note, anything.
missions.ask: What did this help you understand?

missions.title: Show me what you keep beside you
missions.body: Don’t photograph the task. Photograph what’s around it: a certificate, another phone, a notebook, Aadhaar, a printout, another person.

missions.title: Show me who helps
missions.body: Photograph the person, message, screen, note or place that helped you: whatever helped, when something or someone helped.
missions.ask: What did they help you do? Could you have done it alone?

missions.title: Show me when information changes
missions.body: Paper → photo. Photo → PDF. English → explanation. Notice → WhatsApp. Show something you had to change before you could use it.
missions.ask: What did you have to do to make it usable?

missions.title: Show me when the normal way doesn’t work
missions.short: When the normal way doesn’t work
missions.body: Not “what problems did you face”: show us the workaround. Asking someone, another device, a cyber café, a screenshot, a call, a repeat.
missions.ask: What made you do this instead?

missions.title: Show me what you check again
missions.body: Show something you check more than once: before you trust it, before you act on it, before you submit it.
missions.ask: What are you checking for? What makes you feel sure?
